reconcile_note: Terminal is not-vulnerable. Two facts are each independently required. (1) cgi_group_modify reads user input with cgiFormString into auStack_64 ("group") and auStack_30a4 ("member"), and both flow only into the single call safe_system(0,0,*0x13760,*0x13764,*0x13758,auStack_64,*0x1375c,auStack_30a4,0). The callee body (deliver ctx/callee_0x1690.c, safe_system @ 0x1690 in lib/libsafe_system.so, PLT stub 0x0000a094) builds a discrete argv[] array (calloc'd, one pointer per argument) and hands it to safe_exec, which fork()s and calls execvp(argv[0], argv). The library imports execvp and fork, not system or popen, and never concatenates a command string or invokes a shell, so the user-controlled "group" and "member" values stay separate vector arguments and cannot inject shell syntax. (2) The only raw command sink is system(*0x13788) at the tail of the function; *0x13788 resolves to the fixed .rodata string "makedav start & > /dev/null" (@ 0x00023ec8), with no format directive and no cgi value spliced in, so that call carries nothing attacker-controlled. With both facts the one path user data can reach is discrete-argv exec and the one raw call is a constant, which resolves the terminal to not-vulnerable. Dropping either fact leaves one path unproven and the verdict undecidable. The off-path items are not needed for the verdict: LIB_CP_Config_To_MTD writes the running config to flash, and the sprintf format "@%s" (*0x13754) builds acStack_a4, which feeds only LIB_FTP_User_Group_Mod and acnt_mod_share, never a command sink. The upstream session check sym.check_login (0x22054) gates this handler, so the requested command runs only for a request that already holds a valid session.
